data.name: Letras parecidas al latín
data.description: А Е О М Т К В Н Р С — entrada fácil al cirílico

cards.translation:
Name: А (a) — sounds like “a” in “father”
Identical to Latin A
cards.mnemonic: It’s the same as your A, just keep it simple.

examples.t: This is А, just like in mamá
Write А with two strokes: a vertical and a crossbar

cards.translation:
Name: Е (ye) — sounds like “ye” in “yes”
Looks like Latin E but sounds like YE
cards.mnemonic: Think of the English word “yet” — that’s the sound.

examples.t: Say Е as in “yellow” — not like “e”
Е is a letter that always carries a hidden “y” sound

cards.translation:
Name: О (o) — sounds like “o” in “more”
Identical to Latin O
cards.mnemonic: A perfect circle — just like the letter O.

examples.t: This is О, a round letter like a wheel

cards.translation:
Name: М (em) — sounds like “m” in “mother”
Identical to Latin M
cards.mnemonic: Two peaks like a mountain — M.

examples.t: М is the same as your M, no tricks
Think of “mom” — both start with М

cards.translation:
Name: Т (te) — sounds like “t” in “top”
Identical to Latin T
cards.mnemonic: It’s a capital T — crossbar on top.

cards.translation:
Name: К (ka) — sounds like “k” in “kite”
Identical to Latin K
cards.mnemonic: It’s a K with no changes.

examples.t: К is the same as your K — easy

cards.translation:
Name: В (ve) — sounds like “v” in “very”
Looks like Latin B but sounds like V
cards.mnemonic: A B that says “v” — imagine a bee that says “vroom”.

examples.t: Don’t be fooled: В is not a B, it’s a V
Think of “victory” — that’s the sound

cards.translation:
Name: Н (en) — sounds like “n” in “no”
Looks like Latin H but sounds like N
cards.mnemonic: An H that says “n” — like a horse neighing “nay”.

examples.t: Remember: Н is an H that sounds like N

cards.translation:
Name: Р (er) — sounds like “r” in “run” (rolled)
Looks like Latin P but sounds like R
cards.mnemonic: A P that rolls its Rs — like a pirate saying “arrr”.

examples.t: This is Р — it’s a rolled R, not a P
Practice rolling your tongue: Р like in “perro”

cards.translation:
Name: С (es) — sounds like “s” in “sun”
Looks like Latin C but sounds like S
cards.mnemonic: A C that hisses like a snake — “sss”.

examples.n: I want to, but I can't.
I am glad to see you.

data.name: Letras nuevas — sonidos conocidos
data.description: Б Г Д З И Л П Ф Э Ю Я — formas nuevas, sonidos familiares

cards.translation:
Letter Б — sounds like Spanish B (as in bueno).
Uppercase looks like a B with a missing left side.
cards.mnemonic: It's a 'B' but the belly is on the right — like it's turned to face you.

examples.t:
Брат — brother.
The letter looks like a B that lost its left bump.

cards.translation:
Letter Г — sounds like Spanish G (always hard, as in gato).
Looks like an upside-down L or a gamma.
cards.mnemonic: It's a 'gamma' from math — but sounds like a hard G.

examples.t:
Год — year.
Think 'God' minus the 'o' — but means year.

cards.translation:
Letter Д — sounds like Spanish D.
Looks like a house or a triangle on legs.
cards.mnemonic: It's a little house — 'Дом' means house, so Д = house = D.

examples.t:
Дом — house.
Д looks like a house with a roof!

cards.translation:
Letter З — sounds like Spanish S but voiced (like zumbido).
It's a 3 with a flat top.
cards.mnemonic: It's a 3 (tres) — and it sounds like a buzzing 'z'.

examples.t:
Завтра — tomorrow.
З looks like a 3 — think '3 days from now'.

Зима — winter.
З is like a 3 — snow is cold like a '3'? Eh, just remember the shape.

cards.translation:
Letter И — sounds like Spanish I (as in si).
Looks like a backwards N or an upside-down U.
cards.mnemonic: It's an N flipped — and it says 'ee' like the 'i' in 'machine'.

examples.t:
Или — or.
И looks like a backwards N — 'N' for 'or'? Just remember the sound.

cards.translation:
Letter Л — sounds like Spanish L.
Looks like an upside-down V or a tent.
cards.mnemonic: It's a tent (like a camping tent) — and 'lodge' starts with L.

examples.t:
Лес — forest.
Л is a tent — you camp in a forest.

Люди — people.
Л is a tent — people live in tents? Just remember the sound.

cards.translation:
Letter П — sounds like Spanish P.
Looks like the Greek π (pi) with a flat top.
cards.mnemonic: It's a 'pi' (π) — but with a flat top. Pi = P.

cards.translation:
Letter Ф — sounds like Spanish F.
It's a circle with a line through it.
cards.mnemonic: It's an 'F' that swallowed a ball — or a lollipop with a stick.

cards.translation:
Letter Э — sounds like Spanish E but open (like in él), without the 'y' glide.
It's a backwards E (like the Euro sign € without the lines).
cards.mnemonic: It's a backwards E — 'E' for 'Echo' but reversed, sounds like 'eh'.

examples.t:
Это — this is.
Э is a backwards E — 'eh-to' = this.

cards.translation:
Letter Ю — sounds like the English word "you".
It's an I with a hook underneath.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like an I with a little tail — and it says 'you'.

examples.t:
Я тебя люблю — I love you.
Ю = 'you' — you is right there!

cards.translation:
Letter Я — sounds like "ya" as in yacht.
It's a backwards R.
cards.mnemonic: It's a backwards R — and 'R' backwards = 'Я' = 'ya'.

examples.n: There are many trees in the forest.
I live on the fifth floor.

data.name: Sonidos únicos del ruso
data.description: Ж Ш Щ Ч Х Ц Ъ Ь Ы — los sonidos más difíciles

cards.translation:
Sounds like the s in “treasure” or French j.
It’s a buzzing, vibrating sound.
cards.mnemonic: Looks like a beetle with its legs spread. A beetle goes “zhzhzh”.

examples.t: Ж is like the Ж in жить (to live).
It’s never soft, always hard and buzzing.

cards.translation:
Sounds like SH in “shoe”.
It’s a hard, hissing sound.
cards.mnemonic: The shape looks like a comb with three teeth. Comb your hair and say “shhh”.

cards.translation: A soft, prolonged SH — like “sh” but with a smile, as if saying “shee” but longer.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a brush with three bristles. Brush your teeth and say “shhh” with a smile.

examples.n: Hot soup makes you hiss softly.

examples.t: Compare: Ш is hard, Щ is soft.

cards.translation: Sounds like CH in “cheap” but softer, as if you’re whispering.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like an upside-down chair. Sit and say “ch” quietly.

examples.n: Tea is served with a soft ch.
Practice: ч-ч-ч like a quiet train.

cards.translation: Like the j in Spanish “jota” — a strong h from the throat.
cards.mnemonic: Looks like an X. Cross your arms and say “kh” like a Scottish “loch”.

examples.t: No English equivalent, but Spanish j works.

cards.translation: Sounds like ts in “pitza” — a quick burst.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a claw or a crab. A crab snaps “ts-ts-ts”.

examples.n: Prices make you click your tongue.

cards.translation: The hard sign — it has no sound. It separates a prefix from a vowel, making the consonant hard.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a little hook. It hooks two parts together but stays silent.

examples.t: You never hear it, but it changes the sound.
examples.n: Think of it as a silent guard.

cards.translation: The soft sign — it has no sound itself, but it softens the previous consonant (like adding a y sound).
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a soft, round wave. It makes consonants soft and gentle.

cards.translation: A unique vowel between i and u. No English equivalent — like saying “ee” with your tongue pulled back.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a stick with a ball. Imagine a person shrugging and saying “uh-ee”.

examples.t: Practice: Ы is deep, И is high.

examples.n: I want to live in Moscow.
I don't know what to do.
We are going to the congress.

data.name: Primeras palabras rusas
data.description: Leer y entender 20 palabras rusas esenciales
